---
title: "Bias, Variance, and Nonlinear Models"
---

This lecture connects model flexibility to prediction error and then
introduces nonlinear regression tools such as polynomials, step
functions, splines, and generalized additive models.

## Learning Objectives

- Explain the bias-variance tradeoff.
- Identify underfitting and overfitting from train/test patterns.
- Fit polynomial, step-function, spline, and additive models.
- Use validation to choose nonlinear complexity.

## Core Ideas

Increasing flexibility often lowers bias and raises variance. The
practical question is not whether a model is flexible, but whether its
flexibility is earning lower expected test error.

## Worked Example

Use a simulated nonlinear function and a real data example to compare
linear regression, polynomial regression, regression splines, and GAMs.

## Lab

Lab 06 nonlinear regression can become the applied exercise for this
lecture.
